subproblems.title: Constant density on the support forces constant multiplicity
subproblems.statement: For all P, n, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), every integer multiplicity triple R = (S, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n representing T, every p ∈ ℝ^P and every ρ ∈ ℝ: if Θⁿ(μ_T, y) = k (HasMassDensity T y k) for every y ∈ spt T ∩ B_ρ(p), then (a) for μ_R-a.e. x, where μ_R := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞S, x ∈ B_ρ(p) implies θ(x) = k; and (b) θ(x) = k for Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B_ρ(p))-a.e. x. Here Hⁿ := μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (p : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ) (k : ℕ), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ y ∈ T.support, y ∈ ball p ρ → HasMassDensity T y k) → (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, x ∈ ball p ρ → R.mult x = k) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ ball p ρ)), R.mult x = k
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1 and 3. Step 3 identifies θ through the a.e. equality Θⁿ(μ_T, x) = θ(x). That equality is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) (chapter-03.txt, lines 298–313), with μ_T = μ_V by Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3), and the accepted lemma `Submission.rsd_ae_hasMassDensity_mult` encodes it. Conventions: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Hⁿ⌞A := μHE[n].restrict A; S := R.carrier; θ := R.mult (read in ℝ≥0∞ where needed); B := ball p ρ; μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞S).withDensity θ. No assumption on ρ is used: if ρ ≤ 0 then B = ∅, and the argument below covers this case.
1. (spt T carries Hⁿ⌞S.) By the accepted lemma `Submission.imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null` (U open, R represents T), Hⁿ(S ∖ spt T) = 0. S is measurable (field measurableSet_carrier), so Measure.restrict_apply' gives (Hⁿ⌞S)((spt T)ᶜ) = Hⁿ((spt T)ᶜ ∩ S) = Hⁿ(S ∖ spt T) = 0. Hence Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. x lies in spt T.
2. (spt T carries μ.) μ is a withDensity measure over Hⁿ⌞S, so μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞S (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). By step 1, μ-a.e. x lies in spt T.
3. (Conclusion (a).) By the accepted lemma `Submission.rsd_ae_hasMassDensity_mult` (U open, R represents T), HasMassDensity T x θ(x) for μ-a.e. x. Take x with this property and with x ∈ spt T (μ-a.e. x has both, by step 2), and suppose x ∈ B. Then x ∈ spt T ∩ B, so HasMassDensity T x k by hypothesis. The accepted uniqueness lemma `Submission.dimred_cs_mi_hasMassDensity_unique` gives (θ(x) : ℝ) = (k : ℝ), hence θ(x) = k, because the cast ℕ → ℝ is injective. Thus ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ B → θ(x) = k, which is the first conjunct.
4. (Hⁿ⌞S ≪ μ.) The function x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) is measurable: it is field measurable_mult composed with the measurable cast ℕ → ℝ≥0∞. It is nonzero Hⁿ⌞S-a.e., because Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. x lies in S (ae_restrict_mem, S measurable) and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ S (field mult_pos). By withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', Hⁿ⌞S ≪ (Hⁿ⌞S).withDensity θ = μ. Concretely: if A is measurable and μ(A) = ∫_{A∩S} θ dHⁿ = 0, then θ = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on A ∩ S, so Hⁿ(A ∩ S) = 0 because θ ≥ 1 on S.
5. (Conclusion (b).) By steps 3 and 4, x ∈ B → θ(x) = k holds Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. Since S ∩ B ⊆ S, we have Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B) ≤ Hⁿ⌞S (Measure.restrict_mono), so the implication also holds Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B)-a.e. S ∩ B is measurable (S measurable, B open), so Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B)-a.e. x lies in S ∩ B ⊆ B (ae_restrict_mem). Combining the two, θ(x) = k for Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B)-a.e. x, which is the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(S ∖ spt T) = 0 (imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null). Hence Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. points lie in spt T, and so do μ-a.e. points, since μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞S.
μ-a.e. x has density θ(x) (rsd_ae_hasMassDensity_mult). At such x ∈ spt T ∩ B the density is also k, so θ(x) = k by uniqueness (dimred_cs_mi_hasMassDensity_unique). This is conclusion (a).
θ ≥ 1 on S gives Hⁿ⌞S ≪ μ (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous'), so (a) holds Hⁿ⌞S-a.e.
Restrict from Hⁿ⌞S to Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B), under which a.e. point lies in B. This gives conclusion (b).

subproblems.title: Constant positive density puts the support inside the carrier up to an Hⁿ-null set
subproblems.statement: For all P, n, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), every integer multiplicity triple R = (S, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n representing T, every p ∈ ℝ^P and every ρ ∈ ℝ with B_ρ(p) ⊆ U: if k ≥ 1 and Θⁿ(μ_T, y) = k (HasMassDensity T y k) for every y ∈ spt T ∩ B_ρ(p), then Hⁿ((spt T ∩ B_ρ(p)) ∖ S) = 0, where Hⁿ := μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (p : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ) (k : ℕ), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ball p ρ ⊆ U → 1 ≤ k → (∀ y ∈ T.support, y ∈ ball p ρ → HasMassDensity T y k) → μHE[n] ((T.support ∩ ball p ρ) \ R.carrier) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1 and 4. The parent states step 4 for M ∩ B_ρ(p), which equals spt T ∩ B_ρ(p) by its hypothesis; this child proves the support form. The density-zero input is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2) (Upper Density Theorem; chapter-01.txt, lines 700–711) for Hⁿ⌞S, as encoded by the accepted lemma `Submission.regcomp_atl_local_density_zero`. M_W(T) = μ_T(W) is Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3). Conventions: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Hⁿ⌞A := μHE[n].restrict A; S := R.carrier; θ := R.mult; B := ball p ρ; μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞S).withDensity θ; ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : ℝⁿ) 1). All quotients below are in ℝ≥0∞.
1. (Hⁿ⌞S is locally finite in U.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. For x ∈ S ∩ K we have 1 ≤ θ(x) (field mult_pos). Hence Hⁿ(S ∩ K) = ∫_{S∩K} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{S∩K} θ dHⁿ (setLIntegral_mono'; S ∩ K is measurable). The right side is finite by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, so Hⁿ(S ∩ K) ≠ ∞.
2. (Density zero off S.) Apply the accepted lemma `Submission.regcomp_atl_local_density_zero` to U (open) and S (measurable, locally finite by step 1). It gives an Hⁿ-null set Z with the following property. For every x ∉ Z with x ∈ U and x ∉ S, f_x(r) := Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, r)) / (ofReal r)ⁿ → 0 as r → 0⁺.
3. (Multiplicity k.) By the second conjunct of the sibling lemma `Submission.idtp_ccd_sfv_mult_ae_eq_density` (U open, R represents T, density hypothesis), θ(y) = k for Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B)-a.e. y.
4. (The constant ω_n.) ω_n is the volume of a nonempty open ball of ℝⁿ. So 0 < ω_n (measure_ball_pos) and ω_n < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). In particular k/ω_n ≠ ∞.
5. (Key claim.) Let x ∉ Z with x ∈ spt T ∩ B. We show x ∈ S. Suppose not.
   (a) Since B ⊆ U, x ∈ U ∖ S, so f_x(r) → 0 by step 2.
   (b) Since x ∈ spt T ∩ B, HasMassDensity T x k holds. Its second component says g_x(r) := M_{B_r(x)}(T) / (ω_n · ofReal(rⁿ)) → ofReal k as r → 0⁺.
   (c) Put δ := ρ − |x − p|, which is positive because x ∈ B. Fix r ∈ (0, δ). Then B_r(x) ⊆ B ⊆ U (ball_subset_ball', since r + |x − p| ≤ ρ).
   (d) The accepted lemma `Submission.rsd_massOn_eq_measure` (U open, R represents T, B_r(x) open) gives M_{B_r(x)}(T) = μ(B_r(x)).
   (e) By the definition of μ (withDensity_apply with B_r(x) measurable, then Measure.restrict_restrict), μ(B_r(x)) = ∫_{B_r(x) ∩ S} θ dHⁿ. Since B_r(x) ∩ S ⊆ S ∩ B, step 3 gives θ = k Hⁿ⌞(B_r(x) ∩ S)-a.e. Hence μ(B_r(x)) = k · Hⁿ(S ∩ B_r(x)), the integral of a constant.
   (f) Use ofReal(rⁿ) = (ofReal r)ⁿ for r ≥ 0, and a·b/(c·d) = (a/c)·(b/d) in ℝ≥0∞, which holds since ω_n ≠ 0 and ω_n ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_div_mul_comm). Together with Hⁿ(S ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, r)) this gives g_x(r) = (k/ω_n) · (Hⁿ(S ∩ B_r(x)) / (ofReal r)ⁿ) ≤ (k/ω_n) · f_x(r).
   (g) So g_x(r) ≤ (k/ω_n)·f_x(r) for every r in (0, δ), a set in 𝓝[>]0. Since k/ω_n ≠ ∞, (k/ω_n)·f_x(r) → (k/ω_n)·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul).
   (h) 𝓝[>]0 is a nontrivial filter, so passing to the limit in the inequality (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto) gives ofReal k ≤ 0, i.e. (k : ℝ) ≤ 0. This contradicts 1 ≤ k, hence x ∈ S.
6. (Conclusion.) By step 5, (spt T ∩ B) ∖ S ⊆ Z, so Hⁿ((spt T ∩ B) ∖ S) ≤ Hⁿ(Z) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ ≥ 1 on S and locallyIntegrable_mult give Hⁿ(S ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
regcomp_atl_local_density_zero: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ U ∖ S, Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, r))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0.

For such x ∈ spt T ∩ B and 0 < r < ρ − |x − p|, rsd_massOn_eq_measure and sibling mult_const give M_{B_r(x)}(T) = μ(B_r(x)) = k·Hⁿ(S ∩ B_r(x)). So the density ratio is at most (k/ω_n)·Hⁿ(S ∩ closedBall(x, r))/rⁿ, which tends to 0.
The density at x is k ≥ 1 by hypothesis, a contradiction. Hence (spt T ∩ B) ∖ S lies in the Hⁿ-null exceptional set.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded C¹ d-submanifold is a d-dimensional subspace
subproblems.statement: For all P, d ∈ ℕ, every M ⊆ ℝ^P that is an embedded C¹ d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d M) and every x ∈ M, tangentSpace M x is a linear subspace. Precisely, the linear span of tangentSpace M x has carrier exactly tangentSpace M x, and this span has dimension d.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d M → x ∈ M → (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x) : Set (Euclid P)) = tangentSpace M x ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)) = d
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5, last two sentences. This is Simon Ch. 2, §4, (4.3) (chapter-02.txt, lines 865–871): T_yM is a linear subspace with basis D₁ψ(x), …, D_dψ(x) for any local representation ψ with ψ(x) = y.
1. (Chart.) Since x ∈ M and IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d M holds, there are an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P with these properties: ψ is C¹ on V; ψ is injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ M; V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W; and Dψ(z) is injective for every z ∈ V.
2. (Preimage point.) x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), so x = ψ(v) for some v ∈ V.
3. (Tangent space as a range.) Apply the accepted lemma `Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv` with r := 1 (so 1 ≤ r), N := M and the data V, W, ψ, v of steps 1–2. It gives tangentSpace M x = tangentSpace M (ψ v) = range Dψ(v). The first conjunct of the accepted lemma `Submission.dsmc_chart_tangentSpace_eq_range` (r := 1) gives the same identity. Let L := Dψ(v), viewed as a linear map ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Then range Dψ(v) = ↑(LinearMap.range L) (LinearMap.coe_range).
4. (First claim.) LinearMap.range L is a submodule, so span ℝ ↑(LinearMap.range L) = LinearMap.range L (Submodule.span_eq). By step 3, span(tangentSpace M x) = LinearMap.range L. Therefore ↑span(tangentSpace M x) = ↑(LinearMap.range L) = tangentSpace M x.
5. (Dimension.) L is injective (step 1 with z := v). Hence finrank(LinearMap.range L) = finrank ℝ^d = d (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). By step 4, finrank span(tangentSpace M x) = d. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a chart ψ : V → W ∩ M of M at x and v ∈ V with ψ(v) = x.
chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv (r = 1): tangentSpace M x = range Dψ(v), which is the carrier of the submodule LinearMap.range Dψ(v).
Hence span(tangentSpace M x) = LinearMap.range Dψ(v), and its carrier is tangentSpace M x.
Dψ(v) is injective, so finrank (range Dψ(v)) = finrank ℝ^d = d.

subproblems.title: On a carrier lying a.e. inside a C¹ submanifold, the approximate tangent planes are the submanifold's tangent planes
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every integer multiplicity triple R = (S, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n and all M, V ⊆ ℝ^P, assume three things: M is an embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M); V is open; and Hⁿ((S ∩ V) ∖ M) = 0, where Hⁿ := μHE[n]. Then approxTangentPlane n S x = span(tangentSpace M x) for Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V)-a.e. x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (M V : Set (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M → IsOpen V → μHE[n] ((R.carrier ∩ V) \ M) = 0 → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ V)), approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x = Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5. This is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) (chapter-03.txt, lines 86–90): TₓM = TₓN_j for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j when M_j ⊆ N_j and N_j is a C¹ n-submanifold. Conventions: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Hⁿ⌞A := μHE[n].restrict A; S := R.carrier.
1. (Measurability.) S ∩ V is measurable: S by the field measurableSet_carrier, and V because it is open.
2. (Approximate tangent planes exist.) By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q. (The field also gives IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, which is not needed.) Since S ∩ V ⊆ S, Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V) ≤ Hⁿ⌞S (Measure.restrict_mono), so this holds Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V)-a.e.
3. (Points of S ∩ V.) By step 1, Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in S ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem).
4. (Points of M.) Since S ∩ V is measurable, Measure.restrict_apply' gives (Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V))(Mᶜ) = Hⁿ(Mᶜ ∩ (S ∩ V)) = Hⁿ((S ∩ V) ∖ M) = 0 by hypothesis. So Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in M.
5. (Pointwise identification.) Fix x satisfying steps 2–4: a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q, x ∈ S ∩ V and x ∈ M.
   (a) approxTangentPlane n S x = Q by the accepted lemma `Submission.dpf_itt_approxTangentPlane_eq`. Equivalently: Q witnesses the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane; the chosen plane is an approximate tangent space at x, so it equals Q by `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`.
   (b) finrank Q = n. This is the first component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt (`HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq`).
   (c) (Localization.) Apply the accepted lemma `Submission.dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff` with M := S, M' := S ∩ V ⊆ S, the open set V and x ∈ V. Its null-set hypothesis holds because (S ∖ (S ∩ V)) ∩ V = ∅. It gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (S ∩ V) x Q.
   (d) (Containment.) Apply the accepted lemma `Submission.approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace` with these inputs: d := n; N := M, an embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifold; the set S ∩ V in the role of its M; the point x ∈ M; the hypothesis Hⁿ((S ∩ V) ∖ M) = 0; and (c). It gives Q ⊆ tangentSpace M x. Since tangentSpace M x ⊆ span(tangentSpace M x) (Submodule.subset_span), Q ≤ span(tangentSpace M x).
   (e) (Equal dimensions.) By the sibling lemma `Submission.idtp_ccd_sfv_span_tangentSpace_finrank` (d := n, x ∈ M), finrank span(tangentSpace M x) = n, which equals finrank Q by (b). A submodule contained in a finite-dimensional submodule of the same finrank equals it (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). So Q = span(tangentSpace M x).
   (f) By (a) and (e), approxTangentPlane n S x = span(tangentSpace M x).
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 2–4 hold together for Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V)-a.e. x, since a finite intersection of a.e. sets is a.e. Step 5 proves the claimed identity at each such x. ∎
proof_key_steps: For Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ V)-a.e. x: S has an approximate tangent plane Q at x (field orients), x ∈ S ∩ V, and x ∈ M (since Hⁿ((S ∩ V) ∖ M) = 0).
At such x, approxTangentPlane n S x = Q (dpf_itt_approxTangentPlane_eq) and finrank Q = n.
Localize to S ∩ V (dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff). Then approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace gives Q ⊆ tangentSpace M x ⊆ span(tangentSpace M x).
Sibling tangent_space_dim gives finrank span(tangentSpace M x) = n = finrank Q, so Q = span(tangentSpace M x).
